title: Energy transfers and conservation mark scheme

questions.answer: W = Fs = 48 x 3.5 = 168 J. This is 168 J of energy transferred to the box by the pushing force.
accepted_alternatives: Accept 0.168 kJ with a correct statement that work is energy transferred by the force.
questions.unit_policy: J or kJ required for the numerical answer.

marking_points.text: Calculates W = 48 x 3.5 = 168 J
States that the work is energy transferred to the box by the pushing force
Selects C: energy cannot be created or destroyed but can be transferred between stores and across a boundary

option_feedback.A: Work transfers energy; it does not create energy.
option_feedback.B: Energy that becomes less useful is dissipated, not destroyed.
option_feedback.C: Correct. A complete account preserves the total while allowing transfers and store changes.
option_feedback.D: Thermal, deformation, chemical and other stated stores may also be part of the account.

marking_points.text: Selects A: 900 - 610 - 40 = 250 J increases thermal stores

option_feedback.A: Correct. The unaccounted energy is 900 - 610 - 40 = 250 J.
option_feedback.B: This subtracts only the mixture gain and forgets the 40 J sound transfer.
option_feedback.C: This adds the mixture and sound transfers instead of finding the remaining energy.
option_feedback.D: This adds outputs to the input and cannot be a conserved remainder.

marking_points.text: Selects D: the 440 J store increase and 80 J thermal increase account for the 520 J input

option_feedback.A: The flywheel alone is an incomplete account because the bearings also warm.
option_feedback.B: The bearings may be included, and their 80 J store change completes the account.
option_feedback.C: Friction transfers energy to thermal stores; it does not destroy it.
option_feedback.D: Correct. The two stated changes total the full 520 J input.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The input is 1.50 kJ, or 1500 J, transferred from the battery. The stated account includes 920 J received by the drill bit and material and 70 J transferred by sound.
accepted_alternatives: Accept the input in kJ if the stated outputs are identified correctly in J.
parts.unit_policy: Each numerical energy must retain J or kJ.

marking_points.text: Identifies 1.50 kJ from the battery as the energy input
Identifies the stated 920 J bit-and-material change and 70 J sound transfer

parts.label: (b)
accepted_alternatives: Accept 0.510 kJ after a consistent conversion.

marking_points.text: Forms the conservation balance 1500 = 920 + 70 + E_thermal
Obtains an increase of 510 J in the other thermal stores

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Energy leaving the battery is transferred to the bit and material, thermal stores and sound. The complete changes total the battery's 1500 J decrease, so energy is transferred rather than destroyed.
parts.unit_policy: No unit required in a correct verbal explanation.
parts.tolerance: The explanation must refer to transfers or store changes and the complete account.

marking_points.text: Explains that the battery energy is transferred into the stated changes whose total equals 1500 J, rather than being destroyed

parts.label: (a)
parts.tolerance: Exact values 220 J and 410 J required.

marking_points.text: Calculates the thermal-store energy at stage A as 220 J
Calculates the thermal-store energy at stage B as 410 J

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Original-store points: 720, 500, 310, 0 J. Thermal-store points: 0, 220, 410, 720 J. Each set is joined in stage order and both lines are labelled.
accepted_alternatives: Accept a correct point plot with a clear key instead of labels written beside the lines.
parts.unit_policy: The vertical axis must be labelled Energy / J or equivalent.
parts.tolerance: Points should be plotted within half a minor division of their values.

marking_points.text: Plots the original-store values 720, 500, 310 and 0 J at the four stages
Plots the thermal-store values 0, 220, 410 and 720 J at the four stages
Joins consecutive points and distinguishes the two lines with correct labels or a clear key

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: At every stage, original-store energy + thermal-store energy = 720 J.
accepted_alternatives: Accept any one explicit stage sum, such as 500 + 220 = 720 J, if stated as the required conservation check.
parts.unit_policy: J required in a numerical check.

marking_points.text: States or demonstrates that the two store values sum to 720 J at every stage
Uses W = Fs with the 260 N force and 7.5 m displacement
Obtains 1950 J of work done by the winch

parts.label: (b)
accepted_alternatives: Accept 0.120 kJ after a consistent conversion.

marking_points.text: Forms the conservation balance 1950 = 1420 + 410 + E_sound
Obtains 120 J carried away by sound

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: 1950 J input = 1420 J sled-store increase + 410 J thermal-store increase + 120 J sound transfer. The right side totals 1950 J, equal to the work input, so the chosen start-to-end account conserves energy.
accepted_alternatives: Accept the same balance consistently written in kJ.
parts.unit_policy: All terms must use one consistent energy unit.
parts.tolerance: The equality and its interpretation are both required.

marking_points.text: Writes the complete balance 1950 J = 1420 J + 410 J + 120 J
Explains that equality of the total input and all store changes or transfers demonstrates conservation for the chosen states
